claims.claim: Explicitly modeling Gestalt principles will reduce spatial hallucinations by ~30% and improve 3D grounding by 15–20% on ScanNet-derived datasets.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Quantitative effects are predictions without cited evidence; Gestalt operationalization in deep models is an active research area.

claims.claim: NAS-Bench-201 is a standard NAS benchmark suitable for testing architecture search methods.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: Widely used tabular NAS benchmark with enumerated search space and ground-truth accuracies.

claims.claim: Training-free (zero-cost) evaluation proxies can estimate architecture quality without full training.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: A body of work shows proxies like SynFlow/Jacobian correlate with final accuracy sufficiently for NAS pruning.

claims.claim: A 62-dataset framework from learning-curve estimation literature is available and applicable to predictive maintenance workloads.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: There are LCE/HPO benchmark collections, but the specific ‘62-dataset’ framing and its focus on predictive maintenance is not a standard, well-known reference.

claims.claim: Self-consistency across multiple chain-of-thought samples improves reliability of LLM reasoning.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: Self-consistency voting has been shown to improve reasoning accuracy in LLMs across tasks.

claims.claim: MS-FAR will reduce the search space by 60% while achieving 95% of exhaustive-search performance.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: This is a forward-looking quantitative claim without prior empirical support.

claims.claim: Zero-cost proxy NAS methods exist and can be extended to new objectives.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: A body of work on zero-cost proxies (e.g., SNIP/GradNorm-based proxies, TE-NAS/Zen-NAS) is well known in NAS.

claims.claim: GSM8K, MATH, and ScienceQA are established complex reasoning benchmarks for LLMs.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: These datasets are standard for evaluating arithmetic and scientific reasoning in LLMs.

claims.claim: Perplexity-based step importance can guide architecture search for reasoning by identifying salient CoT steps.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Perplexity is a next-token predictive metric; its relationship to causal importance of individual reasoning steps is unvalidated.

claims.claim: Chain-of-thought generation cost can be formulated as a differentiable objective suitable for differentiable NAS.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Token count and discrete generation are not inherently differentiable; a surrogate could be devised, but correlation and stability are unproven.

claims.claim: NAS-discovered architectures will outperform manually designed CoT-enhanced models by 8–12% while reducing token generation costs by 35–40%.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: These are quantitative performance claims without prior empirical support; architecture-only gains of this magnitude on reasoning are unestablished.

claims.claim: A CE-NAS carbon-efficient framework can support 50,000 search iterations over 100+ architectures for LLM-scale reasoning experiments.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Carbon/compute-efficient NAS frameworks exist, but applicability and efficacy at LLM scale for reasoning-focused evaluation are not established here.

claims.claim: CRISPR-based dual epigenetic editing can modulate enhancer accessibility (e.g., via dCas9–p300/KRAB) and promoter DNA methylation (e.g., via dCas9–DNMT3A/TET1).
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: Multiple studies have demonstrated locus-specific chromatin and methylation editing using dCas9 fusions.

claims.claim: Single-cell readouts (scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) can be combined with pooled CRISPR perturbations (Perturb-seq-like) to map regulatory effects at scale.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: Perturb-seq and related methods (e.g., CROP-seq, Perturb-ATAC, Multiome perturbations) exist; joint RNA+ATAC with perturbations is emerging but demonstrated.

claims.claim: Reprogramming efficiency limits arise primarily from failures in nested enhancer–enhancer crosstalk rather than individual enhancer–promoter links.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Mechanistic emphasis on enhancer–enhancer crosstalk as the dominant bottleneck is a hypothesis not yet established.

claims.claim: Screening ~5,000 enhancer–promoter pairs across ~2 million cells with Perturb-seq-style single-cell multi-omics is practical.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Technically plausible but very costly and complex, especially for joint RNA+ATAC readouts at this scale.

claims.claim: Engineering synthetic epigenetic circuits (tunable chromatin remodelers and methylation-sensitive promoters) can produce a 2–3× increase in fibroblast-to-iPSC reprogramming efficiency.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Directional improvement is plausible; the quantitative effect size is unproven.

claims.claim: Targeted dCas9–p300 epigenome editing at pluripotency enhancers will reduce chromatin accessibility by >60%.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: dCas9–p300 recruits a histone acetyltransferase domain that deposits H3K27ac and generally increases enhancer activity and chromatin accessibility, not decreases.

claims.claim: BRD4 is a chromatin remodeler that cooperates with OCT4 at distal enhancers.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: BRD4 is a BET bromodomain chromatin reader/co-activator that binds acetyl-lysines and recruits P-TEFb; it is not a chromatin remodeler (e.g., SWI/SNF, ISWI, CHD).

claims.claim: OCT4 and BRD4 co-occupy super-enhancers of pluripotency genes in ESCs, supporting high transcriptional output.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: Multiple studies show BRD4 enrichment at super-enhancers (including pluripotency loci) and OCT4 occupancy at these regions; BRD4 inhibition disrupts pluripotency gene expression.

claims.claim: BET inhibitors would reinforce a pluripotency ‘chromatin barrier’ during early differentiation and could boost reprogramming efficiency.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: BET inhibition (e.g., JQ1) typically displaces BRD4 from super-enhancers and reduces enhancer activity; effects on ‘reinforcing’ a barrier are logically contradictory and highly context-dependent.

claims.claim: For 2+1D quantum critical systems, the entanglement entropy has a volume-law coefficient at criticality.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: For ground states of local Hamiltonians in d>1, entanglement entropy generally obeys an area law with possible subleading logarithmic terms; volume-law scaling is not expected at zero temperature (exceptions require nonlocal interactions or highly excited states).

claims.claim: The violation of the area law for entanglement entropy at critical points is directly proportional to the topological susceptibility.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: There is no established, general proportionality between entanglement-scaling corrections and topological susceptibility; the latter is well-defined in certain gauge theories but is not a standard control parameter for entanglement in 2+1D topologically ordered systems.

claims.claim: The energy dependence of scattering cross sections at a 2+1D critical point is universally determined by the central charge and the topological entanglement entropy.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: In 2+1D CFTs there is no single central charge governing universal dynamics as in 1+1D; topological entanglement entropy characterizes gapped phases, not critical points. Scattering cross sections are set by correlation functions and critical exponents, not TEE.

claims.claim: Cross-section measurements in ultracold atomic quantum simulators provide a direct probe of the underlying entanglement structure.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Ultracold-atom probes (e.g., Bragg spectroscopy) access dynamical structure factors, while direct entanglement measurements typically require interferometric or randomized measurements. A direct, universal mapping from cross-sections to entanglement is not established.

claims.claim: Hinges in these 3D crystals are described as '4D surface intersections'.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: In a 3D solid, surfaces are 2D and hinges are 1D lines where two surfaces meet; there is no 4D geometric manifold involved.

claims.claim: TaAs or Cd3As2 are cubic Weyl semimetals.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: TaAs is a non-centrosymmetric tetragonal Weyl semimetal; Cd3As2 is a Dirac semimetal (also tetragonal), not a Weyl semimetal and not cubic.

claims.claim: Fabry–Pérot interferometry will show an anyonic statistical phase θ = π/4 for Fibonacci anyons.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: Fibonacci anyons (SU(2)_3) have topological spin θ = 4π/5 for the nontrivial anyon; θ = π/4 is not a Fibonacci value and also does not match Moore–Read (π/8 for σ).

claims.claim: Moore–Read Pfaffian edge theory has chiral central charge c = 3/2.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: The MR state supports a charged boson (c = 1) plus a neutral Majorana mode (c = 1/2), totaling c = 3/2.

claims.claim: Shot-noise measurements can detect fractional charges such as e/2 and e/4.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: Quantum shot-noise is a standard probe of fractional charge in FQH systems; e/4 quasiparticles are widely discussed for ν=5/2 MR states; e/2 excitations can also appear.

claims.claim: 1D hinge channels in higher-order Weyl/Dirac semimetals under strong B can host non-Abelian fractional quantum Hall states at ν = 1/2 and 3/2.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Non-Abelian FQH order is intrinsically 2D; realizing it effectively along a 1D hinge via coupled surfaces and axial anomaly is an unverified, nonstandard mechanism.

claims.claim: The Su–Schrieffer–Heeger (SSH) chain is given as an example of a 2D system alongside the Kitaev honeycomb model.
claims.label: INCORRECT
claims.note: The SSH model is a 1D topological insulator, not 2D; conflating its dimensionality is a factual error.

claims.claim: Topological phase transitions are accompanied by a closing of the bulk energy gap at the critical point.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: For models like SSH and Kitaev honeycomb, bulk gap closing at the transition is well established in the literature.

claims.claim: The Hessian eigenvalue spectrum of the training loss for autoregressive neural networks will show bifurcation patterns at critical points mirroring the bulk gap closing.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: A novel assertion linking optimization landscape geometry to physical criticality; plausible but unverified.

claims.claim: Entanglement entropy extracted from the network’s autoregressive coefficients will show non-analytic critical scaling with an exponent different from conventional order parameters.
claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.note: Entanglement scaling at criticality is known, but obtaining it directly from autoregressive coefficients and claiming distinct exponents is unverified.

claims.claim: Exact diagonalization can generate ground states up to system sizes of about L=20 (spin-1/2 sites), enabling a dataset of ~10,000 ground states across parameters.
claims.label: ESTABLISHED
claims.note: ED up to ~20 spins/fermions is standard; generating many parameterized ground states is computationally feasible.
